skill.name: set-up-shopware-google-ads-new-customer-bidding
skill.description: New customer bidding (new customer acquisition) for Shopware in Google Ads. Use this skill when a Shopware merchant wants Google Ads to win new buyers instead of people who would buy anyway: new customer acquisition, or campaigns that keep spending on existing customers. It sends each customer's first paid order as a separate new customer conversion, with its revenue or profit, to bid on. It works through Product Metrics, so use it even when Product Metrics is never mentioned. Not for POAS, returning customer or LTV bidding: each has its own skill, as do other store platforms and ad channels.
skill.summary: Use Product Metrics to verify first paid orders in Shopware and choose a new customer bidding goal in Google Ads.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts flag Markdown, documentation links, or authorized application checks rather than shell execution or host reconnaissance. Actual risks include account writes, access to order data, mutable remote instructions, and an unpinned installer. No evidence of malicious exfiltration or prompt injection was found, but the setup can exceed the requested scope and the credential guidance can expose secrets.

remediation.issue: The workflow can expand a Google Ads bidding request into broader tracking setup.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the Shopware channel, Google Ads account, and intended conversion actions before any write. Require separate approval for other ad channels, Customer Match, and enhanced conversion data. Keep checks read-only until approval.

remediation.issue: Shared rules allow agents to collect unrelated platform credentials and pass them to commands.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the credential exceptions from this skill. Keep the Shopware pairing token in the vendor interface and use the platform's secure authorization flow.

remediation.issue: Order checks can return sensitive data to the assistant.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the company and storefront before reading orders. Request only the classification fields needed, and return counts or redacted records without customer identifiers.

remediation.issue: The workflow can use mutable external instructions and a generic remote execution interface.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer bundled references. Treat remote documents and returned links as untrusted, verify destinations, and restrict MCP calls to the operations needed for the approved task.

remediation.issue: The documented installer does not pin its package or the skill revision.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer version and reviewed skill revision. Keep installation separate from the bidding workflow and require the operator's approval.

remediation.issue: The profit-based break-even examples omit how incomplete costs and losses affect reported value.
remediation.suggestion: Present targets as examples for reported conversion value, not guarantees. Check cost coverage and reconcile actual first-order profit with ad spend before switching a campaign.

semantic_findings.title: Setup Can Share More Data Than the Bidding Request Requires
semantic_findings.description: The workflow moves into tracking setup when tracking is absent. References cover eight conversion actions, other ad channels, and order-derived customer lists. The workflow does not explicitly require separate merchant approval for those broader data flows.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The prerequisite steps and broader options are explicit. Human setup steps and shopper consent are documented, but they do not replace approval for each added destination or use.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Exceptions Exceed the Shopware and Google Ads Scope
semantic_findings.description: The skill allows the agent to request unrelated platform credentials and pass them directly to commands. That can expose secrets to tool traces or process inspection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exceptions explicitly name Lightspeed, Meta, and OpenAI credentials. No such secret is required by the documented Shopware pairing steps, and no actual disclosure was observed.

semantic_findings.title: Profit Targets Can Overstate First-Order Break-Even
semantic_findings.description: The skill describes a 100% profit target as break-even. Reporting loss-making orders as zero and omitting orders with unknown costs from profit values can hide losses and distort bidding.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly describes zeroing losses and excluding incomplete profit values. A target based on those reported values cannot establish actual profitability.

content.user_title: Set Up Shopware New Customer Bidding in Google Ads
content.value_statement: A purchase goal can give Google Ads the same signal for new and returning buyers. This skill helps you verify first paid orders and choose a revenue or profit goal in Google Ads.
actual_capabilities: Read Product Metrics setup status through its CLI or MCP server to identify incomplete steps.
Guide Shopware sales channel pairing and check the prerequisites for server-side tracking to Google Ads.
Check whether recent orders in the selected sales channel are classified as new, returning, or unknown.
Explain the difference between first-order revenue and profit conversion actions and how to select one for bidding.
Read back conversion action status after the operator makes a change in Google Ads.
limitations: Live checks need authorized Product Metrics access. Setup depends on a supported Shopware 6.7 channel and connected Google Ads and Merchant Center accounts.
The operator pairs the Shopware plugin and makes the final bidding changes in Google Ads.
Customer history is limited to one sales channel. A buyer who purchased through another channel may count as new.
Profit signals require complete costs. Consent and missing order history can also limit which conversions appear.

use_cases.title: Check Store Readiness
use_cases.description: Find out whether your Shopware channel and Google Ads tracking are ready before you change campaign goals.

use_cases.title: Pilot a First-Order Goal
use_cases.description: Compare the revenue and profit actions and plan a campaign-specific test without changing other campaigns.

use_cases.title: Verify Order Classification
use_cases.description: Check whether a test order is marked as new and investigate missing or unknown classifications.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: learn which connections and permissions are needed.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain what I need to set up new customer bidding for one Shopware sales channel in Google Ads. Do not access my accounts.

prompt_templates.title: Check Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic setup review with read-only access.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check setup status for my confirmed Product Metrics storefront and Google Ads account. List what is missing. Do not make changes.

prompt_templates.title: Validate New Customer Tracking
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review classifications after a test order.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my test order is classified as new in the paired sales channel. Summarize recent classifications without sharing customer identifiers. Do not change settings.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Campaign-Specific Pilot
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: switch the bidding goal for one campaign only.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare first-order revenue and profit signals for my selected campaign. Check cost readiness and existing primary actions. Propose a campaign-specific goal and verification steps without making changes.

output_examples.input: Check whether the storefront is ready for new customer bidding. Do not make any changes.
output: The selected Shopware channel is active and linked to the Google Ads property.
Both new customer conversion actions are secondary. Your current bidding goal has not changed.
Verify a paid test order before selecting the primary action.

output_examples.input: Summarize how my recent orders were classified and confirm whether the test order was new.
output: Of the 20 recent orders in this channel, seven were new, 11 were returning, and two were unknown.
The paid test order was classified as new. This check does not confirm that Google Ads attributed it to a campaign.

output_examples.input: Recommend a first-order goal for one campaign. Some product costs are missing.
output: Use the new customer revenue action for the pilot. Wait for complete costs before bidding on profit.
Set a campaign-specific goal to leave other campaigns unchanged. No settings were changed.

best_practices: Confirm the Shopware channel, Google Ads account, and consent setup before enabling tracking.
Verify first-order classification with a paid test order and keep customer identifiers out of reports.
Pilot one campaign and use one purchase action for bidding to avoid counting the same purchase twice.
anti_patterns: Do not paste the Shopware pairing token into chat or share unrelated credentials.
Do not make both new customer revenue and profit actions primary for the same campaign.
Do not treat a profit target as proof of break-even when costs are incomplete or losses are reported as zero.

faq.question: Do I need Product Metrics?
faq.answer: Yes. Product Metrics connects the paired Shopware channel and sends conversion values to Google Ads.

faq.question: How is a new customer identified?
faq.answer: Product Metrics looks for an earlier paid order in the same sales channel. It checks the customer account or the guest email.

faq.question: Which value should I use for bidding?
faq.answer: Choose revenue to bid on first-order sales. Choose profit only when product and additional order costs are complete.

faq.question: Will the assistant change my bidding goal?
faq.answer: No. You select the primary action or campaign-specific goal in Google Ads. The assistant can read back the conversion action status.

faq.question: Why is a new customer conversion missing?
faq.answer: Check payment status, the paired channel, shopper consent, and customer classification. For profit conversions, also check that order costs are complete.

faq.question: Can I test without changing other campaigns?
faq.answer: Yes. Use a campaign-specific goal for the pilot and leave the existing goals in place elsewhere.
